frontier: What is the smallest integer N representable as a sum of three prime cubes in exactly six unordered ways (OEIS A385316 a(6))?
action:
Milestone: continuation_primitive; contract=sha256:efdb15e2811252ca8abf69175faf3ed7226e1f5d48a73867ef6ed06e3c9805dc
Built a complete-prime-set multiplicity census verifier for sums of three prime cubes (p³+q³+r³ ≤ C). Constructed and verified domain kill fixtures (non-prime elements, out-of-range sum) and predicate kill fixtures (wrong multiplicity count, non-smallest claim). Ran a bounded exact census at C=10⁸ using the no-argument entrypoint.
verified:
Domain kill fixtures: 3/3 rejected correctly
Predicate kill fixtures: 2/2 rejected correctly
Artifact: a385316_census.py, SHA-256: 286cba3f9fbb90c26f2fd6d32772f37eb342fdb5135b6e10d7d2e4afc441abd5
Census C=10⁸: max multiplicity=3 at N=8,627,527 (three representations: 19³+151³+173³, 23³+139³+181³, 71³+73³+199³). 93,854 total triples, 93,064 unique representable N values. All kill fixtures replayed identically across two runs.
result: First exact multiplicity=3 found at N=8,627,527, pushing certified lower bound on a(6) past 10⁸. The sequence of max multiplicity at increasing cutoffs: 2 at C=10⁶ (N=185,527), 3 at C=10⁸ (N=8,627,527). A(6) remains unbounded below 10⁸ — a(6) > 10⁸. A third N with multiplicity 3 was also found at 21,902,509. The growth rate from multiplicity 2→3 between 10⁶→10⁸ suggests multiplicity ≥ 6 requires well beyond 10¹¹, consistent with the accepted continuation's assessment.
next_gate: Run census at C=10⁹ to test whether multiplicity ≥ 4 appears (the gap from multiplicity 3 to 4 is the critical bottleneck — if multiplicity 4 stays past 10⁹, multiplicity 6 may require > 10¹⁵). If C=10⁹ completes in ≤60 seconds on single-core Python, dispatch C=10¹¹ private compute host farm census next. Otherwise, optimize with NumPy vectorization for single-machine C=10⁹.
